newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Shimon Peres surprised by silent Argentine Congress.
newsitem.headline: Shimon Peres surprised by silent Argentine Congress.

text.p: Former Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres could not believe his ears when he found himself facing a silent Argentine Congress after a brief address on the Middle East peace process.

"If I tell people at home that a parliament did not have a single question, they would not believe it," Peres said late on Monday after a speech to the Senate, according to statements published on Tuesday by state news agency Telam.
Noble laureate Peres had even gone out of his way to "speak less to allow legislators to ask me what they want."
But an uncomfortable silence followed his speech to more than 30 members of the body.

"It appears as if the deputies and senators are very clear about the Middle East peace process," Vice President Carlos Ruckauf joked to break the silence. "The fact of the matter is that the legislators work a lot and talk little."
Peres is on a visit to Argentina until Wednesday to receive honorary doctorates and meet the leaders of a country that is home to one of the world's largest Jewish communities.

Jews in Argentina have suffered two major attacks in recent times -- a bomb at the Israeli Embassy in 1992 that killed 29 people and one at the AMIA Jewish community centre in 1994 that killed 86. Those responsible for both attacks have not been caught.
